market_summary: Monday 16 Nov: chip stocks led a broad tech selloff ahead of Nvidia's first results under interim CEO Kress. Intraday, the Nasdaq was down about 1.3-1.7% and the S&P 500 about 1%; Micron and Marvell fell about 7% and AMD and Broadcom about 5%. A final close was not confirmed at writing. Weighing on chips: a new US Commerce interim rule restricting remote access to advanced chips, as Trump began a China trip. The 10-year yield was reported near 5.15%, oil eased (WTI near $87) as Gulf exports recovered, and Anthropic's IPO is expected to price Wed 18 Nov at a $70-78 range after an earlier $70-80 range was withdrawn as inaccurate.

headlines: Chips sank Monday: Micron -6.6%, Marvell -6.3%, TSMC -5.6%, Nvidia -4.2%; Nasdaq down about 1.5% intraday.
Nvidia reports Tue after US close (Wed morning AEST) under interim CEO Kress; board reportedly won't reinstate Huang.
US widened AI chip export curbs and tightened remote access via third-country data centres.
Anthropic IPO at $70-78: pricing Wed after US close, trading Thu = Fri 1:30am AEDT.
GPU rents still rising: H100 about $3.10/hr, up 3.3% since Nov 8.
